While recent learning-based stereo matchers achieve state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks, their integration into operational satellite pipelines remains challenging due to differences in viewing geometry and disparity assumptions. In this work, we integrate several modern learning-based stereo matchers, including StereoAnywhere, MonSter, Foundation Stereo, and a satellite fine-tuned variant of MonSter, into the Satellite Stereo Pipeline, adapting the rectification stage to enforce compatible disparity polarity and range. We release the corresponding code to enable reproducible use of these methods in large-scale Earth observation workflows. Experiments on satellite imagery show consistent improvements over classical cost-volume-based approaches in terms of Digital Surface Model accuracy, although commonly used metrics such as mean absolute error exhibit saturation effects. Qualitative results reveal substantially improved geometric detail and sharper structures, highlighting the need for evaluation strategies that better reflect perceptual and structural fidelity. At the same time, performance over challenging surface types such as vegetation remains limited across all evaluated models, indicating open challenges for learning-based stereo in natural environments.
tldr: This paper integrates recent learning-based stereo matching algorithms into a Satellite Stereo Pipeline (S2P), demonstrating improvements in Digital Surface Model accuracy compared to classical methods, while also highlighting limitations in handling challenging surface types like vegetation.
tldr_zh: 该论文将最新的基于学习的立体匹配算法集成到卫星立体流水线（S2P）中，与经典方法相比，证明了数字表面模型精度的提高，同时也强调了处理植被等具有挑战性的表面类型的局限性。
summary_zh: 从卫星影像生成数字表面模型是地球观测中的核心任务，通常使用卫星流程中的经典立体匹配算法来解决，例如卫星立体流程（S2P）。虽然最近基于学习的立体匹配器在标准基准测试中取得了最先进的性能，但由于视角几何和视差假设的差异，将它们集成到操作型卫星流程中仍然具有挑战性。在这项工作中，我们将几种现代基于学习的立体匹配器，包括StereoAnywhere、MonSter、Foundation Stereo以及MonSter的一个卫星微调变体，集成到卫星立体流程中，并调整了校正阶段以强制实现兼容的视差极性和范围。我们发布了相应的代码，以支持在大型地球观测工作流程中可重现地使用这些方法。在卫星影像上的实验表明，在数字表面模型精度方面，相对于基于经典代价体的算法，有持续的改进，尽管常用的指标，如平均绝对误差，表现出饱和效应。定性结果揭示了几何细节的显著改善和更清晰的结构，突显了需要更好地反映感知和结构保真度的评估策略。与此同时，所有评估模型在诸如植被等具有挑战性的地表类型上的性能仍然有限，表明基于学习的立体匹配在自然环境中仍存在开放性挑战。

title: SARe: Structure-Aware Large-Scale 3D Fragment Reassembly
summary: 3D fragment reassembly aims to recover the rigid poses of unordered fragment point clouds or meshes in a common object coordinate system to reconstruct the complete shape. The problem becomes particularly challenging as the number of fragments grows, since the target shape is unknown and fragments provide weak semantic cues. Existing end-to-end approaches are prone to cascading failures due to unreliable contact reasoning, most notably inaccurate fragment adjacencies. To address this, we propose Structure-Aware Reassembly (SARe), a generative framework with SARe-Gen for Euclidean-space assembly generation and SARe-Refine for inference-time refinement, with explicit contact modeling. SARe-Gen jointly predicts fracture-surface token probabilities and an inter-fragment contact graph to localize contact regions and infer candidate adjacencies. It adopts a query-point-based conditioning scheme and extracts aligned local geometric tokens at query locations from a frozen geometry encoder, yielding queryable structural representations without additional structural pretraining. We further introduce an inference-time refinement stage, SARe-Refine. By verifying candidate contact edges with geometric-consistency checks, it selects reliable substructures and resamples the remaining uncertain regions while keeping verified parts fixed, leading to more stable and consistent assemblies in the many-fragment regime. We evaluate SARe across three settings, including synthetic fractures, simulated fractures from scanned real objects, and real physically fractured scans. The results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, with more graceful degradation and higher success rates as the fragment count increases in challenging large-scale reassembly.
tldr: The paper introduces SARe, a structure-aware generative framework for large-scale 3D fragment reassembly that addresses cascading failures in existing methods by explicit contact modeling and inference-time refinement, achieving state-of-the-art performance.
tldr_zh: 该论文介绍了SARe，一种结构感知的生成式框架，用于大规模3D碎片重组。它通过显式的接触建模和推理时细化来解决现有方法中出现的级联失败问题，并实现了最先进的性能。
summary_zh: 3D碎片重组旨在恢复无序碎片点云或网格在通用物体坐标系中的刚性姿态，以重建完整的形状。随着碎片数量的增加，尤其是在目标形状未知且碎片提供微弱语义线索的情况下，该问题变得极具挑战性。现有的端到端方法容易因不可靠的接触推理（尤其是不准确的碎片邻接关系）而导致级联失效。为了解决这个问题，我们提出了结构感知重组(SARe)，这是一个生成式框架，包含用于欧几里得空间装配生成的SARe-Gen和用于推理时精化的SARe-Refine，并显式地进行接触建模。SARe-Gen联合预测断裂表面 token 概率和碎片间接触图，以定位接触区域并推断候选邻接关系。它采用基于查询点的条件化方案，并从冻结的几何编码器中提取查询位置处的对齐局部几何 token，从而产生无需额外结构预训练的可查询结构表示。我们进一步引入了一个推理时精化阶段SARe-Refine。通过使用几何一致性检查来验证候选接触边，它选择可靠的子结构，并在保持已验证部分固定的同时，对剩余的不确定区域进行重采样，从而在多碎片的场景中产生更稳定和一致的装配结果。我们在三种设置下评估了 SARe，包括合成断裂、扫描真实对象模拟断裂和真实的物理断裂扫描。结果表明，SARe 具有最先进的性能，并且在具有挑战性的大规模重组中，随着碎片数量的增加，SARe 的性能退化更为平缓，成功率更高。

title: BadminSense: Enabling Fine-Grained Badminton Stroke Evaluation on a Single Smartwatch
summary: Evaluating badminton performance often requires expert coaching, which is rarely accessible for amateur players. We present BadminSense, a smartwatch-based system for fine-grained badminton performance analysis using wearable sensing. Through interviews with experienced badminton players, we identified four system design requirements with three implementation insights that guide the development of BadminSense. We then collected a badminton strokes dataset on 12 experienced badminton amateurs and annotated it with fine-grained labels, including stroke type, expert-assessed stroke rating, and shuttle impact location. Built on this dataset, BadminSense segments and classifies strokes, predicts stroke quality, and estimates shuttle impact location using vibration signal from an off-the-shelf smartwatch. Our evaluations show that BadminSense achieves a stroke classification accuracy of 91.43%, an average quality rating error of 0.438, and an average impact location estimation error of 12.9%. A real-world usability study further demonstrates BadminSense's potential to provide reliable and meaningful support for daily badminton practice.
tldr: The paper presents BadminSense, a smartwatch-based system that analyzes badminton performance through stroke classification, quality prediction, and impact location estimation using wearable sensor data, demonstrating promising accuracy and usability for amateur players.
tldr_zh: 该论文介绍了 BadminSense，一个基于智能手表的羽毛球性能分析系统。它通过穿戴式传感器数据进行击球分类、质量预测和落点估计，为业余球员提供了有前景的精度和实用性。
summary_zh: 羽毛球运动表现评估通常需要专业教练指导，但业余选手往往难以获得这种指导。我们提出了BadminSense，一个基于智能手表的系统，利用可穿戴传感进行细粒度的羽毛球运动表现分析。通过对经验丰富的羽毛球运动员的访谈，我们确定了四个系统设计需求以及三个指导BadminSense开发的实现思路。随后，我们收集了12名有经验的业余羽毛球运动员的羽毛球击球数据集，并标注了细粒度的标签，包括击球类型、专家评估的击球等级和羽毛球击球位置。在此数据集的基础上，BadminSense利用商用智能手表中的震动信号，对击球进行分割和分类，预测击球质量，并估算羽毛球击球位置。我们的评估表明，BadminSense的击球分类准确率达到91.43%，平均质量等级误差为0.438，平均击球位置估算误差为12.9%。一项真实场景的可用性研究进一步证明了BadminSense在日常羽毛球练习中提供可靠且有意义支持的潜力。
